title: Substructures in the Keplerian disc around the O-type (proto-)star G17.64+0.16
question: Does the disc around the O-type (proto)star G17.64+0.16 show substructure, Keplerian rotation, and gravitational stability when resolved at ~20 mas (~40 au)?

data.angular_resolution: 20x15 mas (44x33 au), PA -88.4 deg, continuum robust 0.0

what.value: Radio-to-mm free-free extrapolation: 3.57 to 29.5 mJy at mm wavelengths

evidence.quote: we reported that the radio wavelength emission accounts for between 3.57 mJy and 29.5 mJy when extrapolated to the mm regime.
A point source assumption is consistent with the size (29 mas at 43 GHz) found by (cite: Menten2004)

what.value: Dust opacity kappa = 1.0 cm2/g at 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: we use $\kappa_\nu$ = 1.0 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ as suggested for dust with thin ice mantles

what.value: Stellar parameters of a 45 Msun O star (R0~9.3 Rsun, L~1.9e5 Lsun, T~60000 K)

evidence.quote: temperature of a 45 M$_{\odot}$ main-sequence O-star from (cite: Hosokawa2009)

recipe.goal: Image continuum and measure disc size, inclination
recipe.method: Fit ellipse to the 50 sigma contour; inclination from axis ratio assuming a circular thin disc
assumptions: Circular thin disc with settled mm grains

recipe.goal: Subtract free-free point source and estimate disc mass
recipe.method: Point-source subtraction in visibilities at the upper-limit free-free flux; optically thin mass with Hildebrand formula, Td = 50, 100, 150 K
assumptions: gas-to-dust 100, kappa=1.0 cm2/g at 1.3 mm, Td 50-150 K, d=2.2 kpc

recipe.goal: H2O moment maps and PV diagram
recipe.method: Moment 0/1 maps; PV cut at PA 25.9 deg, 5 pixel width, PA from Gaussian centres of blue and red moment-0 maps
Disc-only Keplerian PV model matched by eye to contours, outer radius 120 au, inclination 40 deg, inner radius 25-30 au
Q = c_s kappa/(pi G Sigma); Sigma from column density times mu m_H, mu=2.3; T(R) propto R^-0.4 anchored to a 45 Msun O star
assumptions: Optically thin; steeper T profile or optical depth would lower Q

evidence.quote: The peak flux is 25.12 mJy beam$^{-1}$
We recover an integrated flux of 79.14 mJy (within a 60 mas radius circle)
we estimate the disc inclination as $\sim$40$\pm$4$^{\circ}$
resulting lower limit optically thin disc mass ranges from 0.6 to 2.6 M$_{\odot}$
the modelled central mass must be increased to 45$\pm$10 M$_{\odot}$
has the lowest Toomre Q values, between 2 and 4

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN threshold, masks, cell and image sizes, deconvolver
Line-free channels used for continuum subtraction
Exact point-source flux subtracted in the visibility domain for the min/max free-free cases
Model parameters of the PV disc model (velocity/density laws, line width) and code
Column density map details and conversion to Sigma
score_reason: Single public dataset with clear weighting and calibration, but the model and imaging details are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Public data and numeric results (continuum fluxes, inclination, disc mass), though the PV mass fit is by eye.
